propositions: A concurrent commit to the shared worktree between verify and sign steps causes HEAD to resolve to different SHAs, causing the signer to refuse attestation but the close to proceed regardless, leaving the ticket permanently closed without a completion signature.
The verify and sign steps independently read HEAD instead of pinning a single revision for the entire verify→sign→close unit, making them vulnerable to interleaving by unrelated concurrent commits.
The suggested recovery (re-close to certify) is a no-op because the ticket is already closed, and only --force-close or manual manifest fabrication are available, neither of which is acceptable.

On detect drift between verified and signed revisions, the close should either pin the verified revision through signing or abort and leave the ticket in_progress for retry, rather than proceeding with an unsigned close.
